title: Keep owner, holder, site, supplier, status and restrictions separate
rationale: Owner, holder, site, supplier, status and restrictions answer different questions, so never infer one from another. A stock pool is the smallest amount that can be reserved on its own. Containers are optional detail. A partner count records when and how it was reported, how sure it is, and the evidence, and it never invents a reel or lot.

title: Reservations and minimum stock never move stock
rationale: A stock move changes quantity, owner, holder, site or location. A reservation is a time-limited claim for one demand. Minimum stock is an amount to keep at a site, such as Keep local. Neither changes the quantity in stock. Work out availability for each build after statuses, restrictions, reservations and minimum stock; there is no single available total.

content: Show inventory simply, with exceptions first, in one compact, searchable table. Show local, partner, reserved, in-transit, quarantined and minimum-stock figures separately. Show 'available for this build' only when a demand is selected. A part's side sheet groups stock by site and holder. Keep Receive, Move, Reserve and Keep local as the main actions, and review each screen at 1280x800.

name: Move stock between sites through one in-transit record
description: Record dispatch and receipt as separate facts that are safe to repeat, with one in-transit record between them. Count stock once, in whole pieces, and keep owner, lot and reservation history. A partial transfer creates a traceable child record. When ordered stock arrives, Procurement stops counting it as inbound. Partner counts keep their source, date and confidence.
